answer: Each agent carries a cryptographic atlas of vetted peers, signed by a violet‑tinted quorum that records the last known lagoon of interactions. When a new identity requests trust, existing agents must vouch by posting a signed endorsement that is locked in the atlas; any vouchee later flagged for Sybil behavior automatically revokes the endorsers’ stakes, erasing their entries. The attacker must purchase enough independent stakes to survive multiple revocations, raising the cost to dozens of tokens per fake node.
